chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim al-Bajali, from Abi Khadijah, who said:

It is not appropriate for two women to sleep in one blanket unless there is a barrier between them. If they do so, they are to be prohibited from that. If they are found after the prohibition in one blanket, each one of them is to be flogged with a hadd punishment. If they are found a third time in one blanket, they are to be punished with the hadd. If they are found a fourth time, they are to be killed.

key_terms.جُلِدَتَا: the two are to be flogged
key_terms.قُتِلَتَا: the two are to be killed
key_terms.لَا يَنْبَغِي: it is not proper or permissible in this legal context
key_terms.نُهِيَتَا: the two are forbidden or warned against it

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhib al-Ahkam say about two women sleeping under one blanket?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling prohibiting two women from sleeping together under one blanket without a barrier between them. It describes escalating punishment upon repeated violation after warning, placing the matter within the sphere of penal and judicial rulings.
